source: Hacker News Search API powered by Algolia
unit: One top-level comment is one employer posting; a posting may advertise multiple roles.

classification.software_pattern: \b(?:software|developer|devops|site reliability|sre|backend|back-end|front[- ]?end|full[- ]?stack|web engineer|mobile engineer|ios engineer|android engineer|data engineer|machine learning engineer|ml engineer|ai engineer|platform engineer|cloud engineer|infrastructure engineer|security engineer|qa engineer|test automation|embedded engineer|firmware engineer|engineering manager|technical lead|tech lead|solutions architect)\b
classification.junior_pattern: \b(?:junior|jr\.?|intern|internship|new grad(?:uate)?|graduate role|entry[- ]level|early career|apprentice(?:ship)?|university hire|0[-– ]2 years|1[-– ]2 years)\b
classification.senior_pattern: \b(?:senior|sr\.?|staff|principal|distinguished|engineering manager|director of engineering|head of engineering|software architect|solutions architect|technical lead|tech lead|team lead|lead (?:software|backend|back-end|front[- ]?end|full[- ]?stack|platform|data|ml|ai|mobile|security|infrastructure|cloud) engineer|(?:5|6|7|8|9|10)\+? years(?: of)? experience)\b
classification.mixed_rule: A software posting matching both junior and senior terms is flagged in both mention counts and labeled mixed.

limitations: Hacker News is a self-selected technology community, not a representative job board.
Keyword classification measures mentions, not the number of distinct vacancies.
A top-level employer comment can contain multiple roles and seniority levels.
Deleted comments and roles described without matching terms may be missed.
